summary: Describes an IMAP extension for sorting messages on the server by the displayed part of the From and To header fields, such as a person's name. It is a Proposed Standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This IMAP extension lets a server sort messages using the name shown for the first From or To address. If no display name is available, the sort uses the mailbox address instead.

questions: how does imap sort by display name
subtitle: IMAP sort criteria that use displayed names in From and To addresses.

tldr.problem: The existing IMAP SORT FROM and TO criteria order messages by the mailbox part rather than the displayed name.
tldr.mechanism: DISPLAYFROM and DISPLAYTO use the first address's display name when available and otherwise fall back to mailbox data.
tldr.outcome: The extension adds the SORT=DISPLAY capability and updates RFC 5256.

today: RFC 5957 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5256. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Sorting by the Name People See
sections.content:
The IMAP SORT extension provides server-side message sorting. Its FROM and TO criteria sort lexically on the mailbox part of the first address in the corresponding header.

This RFC adds DISPLAYFROM and DISPLAYTO, which use the first address's display name when present. A server supporting SORT and both new criteria advertises SORT=DISPLAY.
sections.plainLanguage: The new criteria sort by the displayed name rather than only the mailbox part. The server announces support with SORT=DISPLAY.

sections.title: How an Address Gets a Sort Value
sections.content:
If an address has a display name, the server decodes encoded words and converts the text to a charset valid for the active collation, defaulting to UTF-8. If that value is empty, or no display name exists, the server falls back to mailbox-at-host, then mailbox alone, and finally the empty string.

DISPLAYFROM uses the first address in the envelope's from value; DISPLAYTO uses the first address in the envelope's to value. If the selected envelope value is NIL, the sort value is empty.
sections.plainLanguage: The server uses the decoded display name when it is available. Otherwise it uses the email address, or an empty value if neither is present.

sections.title: Collation, Security, and Registration
sections.content:
The criteria sort strings using the active collation. They use the full decoded display name and do not try to identify a meaningful substring such as a surname.

The author says the capability adds no new security issues. The RFC registers SORT=DISPLAY in the IMAP capabilities registry.
sections.plainLanguage: Sorting compares the full decoded name, not a guessed part of it. The RFC says the added capability does not change IMAP security considerations.
